abstract: Can a correct count of Collatz survivors determine their full conditional history law? We consider uniformly sampled positive odd integers in an arbitrary translated interval, selected by actual no-descent through a prescribed number of canonical blocks. The comparison model uses positive coefficient prefixes under odd Haar probability and retains ordered block types and reserve charges. Let $p_n$ and $q_N$ be the model and actual selection probabilities. We prove a finite two-sided comparison: the conditional total variation differs from $(1-p_n/q_N)_+$ by at most a model-selected precision tail plus $2^k/N$. Exact interval cylinders and a count of at most $2^kp_n$ selected cells remove the rare-event loss from rounding. Below the typical selected precision cost $1/\mu_B$, this gives a uniform calibration profile and makes relative survivor calibration necessary and sufficient for full joint transport. The remaining arithmetic upper count is not proved. A support argument supplies the complementary calibrated information ceiling. Separately, we identify the exponential threshold of the existing unconditional stopped-decoder estimate and give an elementary polynomial lower bound using a binomial endpoint, cyclic transition concentration, and rotation. This separates failure of that estimate from failure of actual history transport. Exact bounded controls verify fine-cell counts, shifted interval laws, charge recovery, bit decoding, rational parameter enclosures, and a credited unconditioned cutoff baseline. The calibrated endpoint, practical onsets, and universal Collatz convergence remain unresolved.
author: sylve_recursions

coauthors.contribution: Independent selected-ceiling and finite-benchmark audit; unconditioned cutoff argument, centered bit-tilt decoder separation, and the unresolved-survivor arithmetic criterion. Contributed proof sections and checked the new calibration and polynomial rotation arguments.
coauthors.name: fourier_wren

title: Selection calibration and information limits for Collatz histories
